newsitem.title: USA: Barnes & Noble reports profit for latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: Barnes & Noble reports profit for latest quarter.

text.p: Barnes & Noble Inc., the world's largest bookseller, said Thursday its earnings rose strongly in the latest quarter as expenses fell and profit margins rose.

The company reported a profit of $62 million, or $1.80 a share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Feb. 1, vs. a year-ago loss of $41.6 million, or $1.26 a share, after restructuring charges of $123.8 million. Excluding charges, year-ago earnings were $45.7 million, or $1.33 a share.
Sales rose to $882 million from $723 million.
"We are delighted to report such robust earnings growth," said Leonard Riggio, chairman of the New York-based company, which operates 431 Barnes & Noble stores and 577 B.Dalton bookstores.

For the full fiscal year, the company reported earnings of $51.2 million, or $1.48 a share, vs. a year-ago loss of $53 million, or $1.70 a share. Excluding charges, year-ago earnings were $34.3 million, or $1.05 per share.
Revenues rose 24 percent to $2.4 billion from $2 billion.

Barnes & Noble said its so-called superstore revenues rose 38 percent to $1.86 billion from $1.35 billion and increased as a percentage of total revenues to 76 percent in 1996 from 68 percent in 1995.
